title: octopus_facts
emotional_arc: Curiosity to amazement and delight at octopus anatomy facts

characters.name: boy_a
characters.visual_description: Boy with brown hair in casual clothes

characters.name: girl_a
characters.visual_description: Girl with blonde hair in red sweater

scenes.speaker: boy_a
scenes.dialogue_line: Hey, did you know that an octopus has three hearts?
scenes.action: Boy asks Girl about octopus hearts with a counter graphic

scenes.speaker: girl_a
scenes.dialogue_line: Wait, what? Three hearts? Why would it need that many?
scenes.action: Girl reacts with shock and curiosity

scenes.speaker: boy_a
scenes.dialogue_line: Two hearts pump blood to its gills, and the third pumps blood to the rest of its body.
scenes.action: Boy explains how the hearts divide their pumping work

scenes.speaker: girl_a
scenes.dialogue_line: That's crazy! Is there anything else unusual about it?
scenes.action: Girl is amazed and asks what other unusual traits it has

scenes.speaker: boy_a
scenes.dialogue_line: Absolutely! An octopus has one central brain, but about two-thirds of its neurons are in its eight arms.
scenes.action: Boy reveals neurons count and eight arms

scenes.speaker: girl_a
scenes.dialogue_line: So its arms can sense things and control many movements almost independently?
scenes.action: Girl concludes that each arm operates semi-independently

scenes.speaker: boy_a
scenes.dialogue_line: Exactly! And its blood is blue because it uses a copper-based protein to carry oxygen.
scenes.action: Boy explains copper protein causing blue blood

scenes.speaker: girl_a
scenes.dialogue_line: Three hearts, eight clever arms, and blue blood? The ocean is full of surprises!
scenes.action: Girl wraps up with a cheerful laughing punchline
